FFESD Fusion and Fission Energy and Science Directorate KW/hr Kilowatts per hour HPC High Performance Computing ORNL Oak Ridge National Laboratory vi EXECUTIVE SUMMARY This report evaluates the benefits of decommissioning six legacy FFESD purchased HPC clusters and consolidating services and workloads into a new HPC cluster named HELIOS. The findings demonstrate significant reductions in the data center power and cooling requirements, data center footprint, and operational overhead, while simultaneously increasing computational capacity. CLUSTER OVERVIEW In the summer of 2023, FFESD purchased new infrastructure, compute, and storage hardware to consolidate the aging FFESD clusters into a single offering. This new cluster, deployed and managed by ITSD HPC, was named HELIOS. Consolidating not only hardware resources but also user data and software required careful design, deployment, and testing before the cluster came online in the fall of 2024. Once HELIOS was fully functional and supporting user needs, the project of decommissioning the older cluster hardware began. Known as the “Legacy Clusters”, there were six clusters that had to be reviewed, inventoried, and its hardware excised. The final cluster, ROSS, was excised from the data center on May 20, 2025. Table 1 lists all FFESD Legacy Clusters, purchase and end dates; however, the findings and analyses in this report are based only on the six clusters that remained - APOLLO, ARTEMIS, LIBBY, LILLI, ROMULUS, and ROSS - when Helios became available for service.
